# A context provider's value is evaluated in the scope enclosing it, so
# `depth(depth + 1)` reads the value it is overriding and nesting accumulates.
#
# The interpreter honours providers itself -- passContext does not run for a
# target with no host language, the same reason `for ... else` and a boundary
# are answered there -- and it walked a provider's children without ever
# evaluating its value. So on `none` a provider set nothing at all and every
# read beneath one answered the context's default: 0 and 0 here, and 0 for the
# plain `depth(7)` below, which is the half that had nothing to do with
# self-reference.
#
# The lowered targets are testdata/context_provider_reads_enclosing.txtar; this
# is the claim a golden cannot make, because it has to run.

sngl test --platform none nested.sngl
stdout 'ok'
sngl test --platform none plain.sngl
stdout 'ok'

-- nested.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

context #depth(0)

component probe node {
    depth(depth + 1) {
        text #one(value="{depth}")
        depth(depth + 1) {
            text #two(value="{depth}")
        }
    }
}

func testAccumulates(t Test, c probe) {
    t.assert(c.one.value == "1")
    t.assert(c.two.value == "2")
}

window {
}
-- plain.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:test"

context #theme("light")

component probe node {
    theme("dark") {
        text #inner(value="{theme}")
    }
    text #outer(value="{theme}")
}

func testProviderApplies(t Test, c probe) {
    t.assert(c.inner.value == "dark")
    t.assert(c.outer.value == "light")
}

window {
}
